text:
Looking at the diff: the `case 'hour':` label is removed and replaced with `case '':`.

Two observations:

1. **`case '':` is dead code.** The regex `/^(-?(?:\d+)?\.?\d+) *(milliseconds?|msecs?|...)?$/i` either matches a non-empty unit alternative in group 2 or leaves group 2 as `undefined` (handled by `(match[2] || 'ms')`). `match[2]` can never be the empty string, so adding `case '':` changes nothing.

2. **Removing `case 'hour':` is a real regression.** In ms@2.1.3, `ms('1 hour')` parses with `match[2] === 'hour'`, which previously fell into the hours case and returned `3600000`. After the change, `'hour'` matches no case label (only `'hours'`, `'hrs'`, `'hr'`, `'h'`, and the dead `''` remain), so execution hits `default: return undefined;`. Callers now get `undefined` from `ms('1 hour')` instead of `3600000`. The library's own suite only tests plural/abbreviated forms (`'2 days'`, `'1h'`, etc.), which is why it still passes.

The singular forms for every other unit (`'minute'`, `'second'`, `'day'`, `'week'`, `'year'`) are all still present — only `'hour'` was dropped, confirming this is an accidental removal rather than an intentional simplification.

```json
{"defect": true, "testFile": {"path": "proof-test.js", "content": "var assert = require('assert');\nvar ms = require('./');\n\ndescribe('proof', function () {\n  it('parses the singular unit \"hour\"', function () {\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('1 hour'), 3600000);\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('2 hours'), 7200000);\n  });\n});\n"}, "note": "The change deletes the `case 'hour':` label (swapping in a dead `case '':` that the regex can never produce, since match[2] is either a non-empty unit or undefined). Consequently ms('1 hour') now falls through to `default` and returns undefined instead of 3600000."}
```
